Cache
Code Cache
DawnGraphiteCache
DawnWebGPUCache
GPUCache

Hi @rekram1-node @jlongster ! 👋

Sorry to ping you directly, but this PR fixes a real blocker for anyone running OpenCode against local models via vLLM (e.g. Kimi k2.6, Qwen 3.5, GLM 5.1).

The issue: LLMs on vLLM frequently emit truncated/malformed JSON in tool call arguments, which causes the session to abort with an "Unterminated string" error. The fix simply wires `jsonrepair` (already in package.json) into the AI SDK's `experimental_repairToolCall` hook — it's a ~15-line change that handles unterminated strings, missing braces, trailing commas, etc.

It has been tested successfully by several users over the past weeks and just had its merge conflicts resolved against latest `dev`.

Would really appreciate a quick look when you have a moment. Thanks! 🙏

Did a focused review of this against the other in-flight workflows effort (#29059 / PR #29789) since they overlap heavily.

**Finding: these two PRs are not independent — #32167 is a genealogical superset of #29789.** `git merge-base --is-ancestor` confirms VasyaYovbak's PR #29789 is fully in the history of this branch; the identical migration timestamps (`20260531160000_workflow-runs`, `…directory`, `…paused_resume`) are the giveaway. So the 80-file overlap isn't two teams duplicating work — it's the workflow subsystem from #29789 plus this PR's nested-spawning + p2 hardening layered on top. Of the shared files, 28 are byte-identical and 52 are this branch's evolution of them.

Net: there is no 3-way reconciliation to do. The orchestration core is one lineage; the only real question is **scope of what lands upstream**, which is exactly what you asked.

**Design-review take:**
- The `ctx.agent` / `parallel` / `pipeline` / `setPhase` shape matches Claude Code's dynamic-workflows runtime closely, and routing `ctx.agent` through real opencode sessions/subagents (so each step is inspectable in the existing tool-call UI) is the right call — better than CC's opaque runtime. The per-step `schema` (structured output), `isolation: "worktree"`, `onError`, per-step `tools`/`skills`/`model`/`variant` are all genuinely useful and have no equivalent yet.
- Strongly agree with your own instinct to **split**: (1) nested spawning + the four guardrails + ask-routing-to-root (#23091/#13715 fixes) is small, high-value, and reviewable on its own; (2) the workflow subsystem (~most of the 55k LoC) as a separate PR. Landing (1) first de-risks the whole thing and the bugfixes are wanted regardless of whether the orchestration layer is accepted.
- One concern worth flagging for review: 55k LoC with generated SDK/openapi churn (`types.gen.ts` alone is ~12k of the diff) makes review hard — separating generated artifacts from hand-written code in the split would help a lot.

**Consolidation branch:** I rebased this onto current `dev` (tip `de9aa9c8`) to confirm it still applies — **merges clean, zero conflicts**: https://github.com/dzianisv/opencode/tree/feat/workflows-consolidated . Since #32167 already contains #29789, that branch is effectively the unified work refreshed on latest `dev`. (I couldn't run `bun turbo typecheck` locally — disk-space limit on my box, not a code issue — but the merge is conflict-free and you reported 23/23 + ~280 tests green.)

Happy to help with the nested-spawning-first split if that's the direction.

Heads-up for anyone tracking this: there are now **two** in-flight efforts, and they're the same lineage rather than competing rewrites.

- **PR #29789** (this issue) — the original project-local workflows: `.opencode/workflows/`, `@opencode-ai/plugin/workflow`, `ctx.agent`/`parallel`/`pipeline`, `/workflow` + `/workflows` TUI, persisted run history.
- **PR #32167** (#32166) — **builds directly on top of #29789** (`git merge-base --is-ancestor` confirms #29789 is in its history; same migration timestamps). It adds nested sub-agent spawning (depth ≤5), worktree isolation, an approval gate, headless `opencode run --workflow`, an `ultracode` keyword, and p2 hardening.

So #32167 is a genealogical superset of this PR — the workflow core here is preserved and evolved, not discarded.

I put up a consolidation branch that takes the superset and refreshes it onto current `dev` (tip `de9aa9c8`) — **merges clean, zero conflicts**: https://github.com/dzianisv/opencode/tree/feat/workflows-consolidated

Given the relationship, the cleanest path forward is probably to land the nested-spawning bugfixes from #32167 first (they fix #23091/#13715), then the workflow subsystem from this lineage as a focused follow-up. cc @VasyaYovbak

I reproduced this on the latest `dev` branch using `bun dev serve`. The main failing path is the Web UI style request shape: the user message contains `text + agent + file`, where `@vision` is sent as an `agent` part, not a `subtask` part. ## Reproduction ### 1. Create a session ```http POST http://localhost:4096/session Content-Type: application/json { "agentID": "build" } ``` This returned session `ses_13f04e5f9ffeU50f57Km5Zc5Yb`. ### 2. Send one message containing `@vision` and an image attachment ```http POST http://localhost:4096/session/ses_13f04e5f9ffeU50f57Km5Zc5Yb/message Content-Type: application/json { "model": { "providerID": "deepseek", "modelID": "deepseek-v4-pro" }, "parts": [ { "type": "text", "text": "@vision describe this image" }, { "type": "agent", "name": "vision", "source": { "value": "@vision", "start": 0, "end": 7 } }, { "type": "file", "url": "data:image/png;base64,...", "mime": "image/png", "filename": "image.png" } ] } ``` The request payload shows the expected `text + agent + file` shape: ### 3. Inspect the stored session messages ```http GET http://localhost:4096/session/ses_13f04e5f9ffeU50f57Km5Zc5Yb/message ``` The stored message history shows that the parent session received the image together with the `agent` part: ### 4. Inspect the server log for this request The relevant log block for the same request is: ```text level=INFO message=process session.id=ses_13f04e5f9ffeU50f57Km5Zc5Yb messageID=... level=INFO message=stream providerID=deepseek modelID=deepseek-v4-pro session.id=ses_13f04e5f9ffeU50f57Km5Zc5Yb small=false agent=build mode=primary ... level=INFO message="exiting loop" session.id=ses_13f04e5f9ffeU50f57Km5Zc5Yb ``` The log shows the parent session runs on `deepseek-v4-pro`, but there is no child session creation and no `vision` subagent execution in the same request path: ## What this confirms This reproduces the issue on the main path that users hit from the app: 1. The user message contains an image attachment. 2. The `@vision` mention is persisted as an `agent` part. 3. The parent session processes the request with the primary model (`deepseek-v4-pro` in this repro). 4. The log does not show a `vision` child session being created or streamed for this request. So the image is admitted into the parent message, but it does not make it into a multimodal `vision` subagent turn. ## Root cause There are two gaps in the current flow. First, the app builds the request as `text + agent + file`: - `packages/app/src/components/prompt-input/build-request-parts.ts` The backend then handles the `agent` part by appending synthetic text instructing the parent model to call the `task` tool: - `packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts:957` - `packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts:968` That means this path goes through the parent model first. It is not a direct `subtask` admission path. Second, `TaskTool.execute`

The font itself is a property of the emulator, not of the running terminal. xterm defined a control sequence for changing fonts [1], but most modern terminal emulators don't support it (iterm2, alacritty, kitty, and others). There's an open issue on WezTerm from 2023 discussing it [2].

[1] https://www.xfree86.org/current/ctlseqs.html (P s = 5 0 → Set Font to P t )

This issue frames the switcher around a `Light` mode for small/local models. The same opt-in selector also solves the high-capability end — and #10927 (overspecification degrading reasoning in capable models), which is cited above, is exactly the case I have data for.

I prototyped a `Frontier` mode (the same idea as `Light`, just a different target): a prompt variant that pushes GPT/Claude-class models toward root-cause reasoning instead of "looks fine" conclusions. Measured with a within-session controlled A/B on a public code-review task (planetiler, last 10 commits, known seeded regressions) — same model, same agent prompt, same session, only the system prompt swapped:

| bug (public-API silent semantic change) | baseline | frontier |
|---|:-:|:-:|
| reservoir polygon dropped | 16.7% | 62.5% |
| signed→unsigned comparison | 16.7% | 87.5% |
| compareTo ordering change | 0% | 50% |
| false positives | 0 | 0 |

~45–71pp better recall at the same (zero) false-positive rate.

This reinforces the case for the switcher being a general mechanism rather than a single `Light` mode: the same option naturally carries `Light` (trim for small models) and `Frontier` (elevate for capable models), with `Default` unchanged.

I have a working branch for the `Frontier` end — the selector mechanism (~30 lines), two prompt files, unit tests, and an Apache-2.0 NOTICE for principles paraphrased from the Codex CLI prompts. Happy to adapt it to whatever config shape the maintainers prefer here (a `mode`/`variant` enum), or open a PR if there's interest in landing the mechanism with `Default` + one alternate to start.

>  Add explicit bash: { "gh *": "allow", "glab *": "allow" } permission rules to the plan agent config

Please don't. I don't want my planning agent to execute any sort of commands, especially not those that can make irreversible changes to remote systems. 

This is a really bad solution.

What is it exactly that you want to fix? Why is it not good enough to clearly tell your agent that the plan is to build a plan, and execution is persisting the plan? I do that all the time and I never had any problem with it starting to implement it. 

I'm already not happy that ANY sort of bash command execution is possible in planning mode. Agents can and will make mistakes, and planning is about collecting information, not outputting. The only output is the plan itself, but even if you want a solution where that plan ends up on a remote service, there could be so much better solutions than giving an agent full access to certain CLI tools and the ability to execute a possibly dangerous commands. 

If you really need your agent to access existing tickets to do the planning, whitelisting gh and glab fully is still not a good solution. There are MCPs that can give finetuned access, and maybe what we need is a set of configuration that allows certain tools to be accessed during planning.

This overlaps with:
- #22067: `/tree` command for visual session navigation
- #23028: Show subagent model in session tree

- `/thread` creates threads from *selected text* (not forking from a message)
- `/graph` is a simpler dialog showing threads + subagents (not full ASCII art tree)
- ThreadFooter with parent/prev/next navigation is new

The `/tree` command in #22067 could potentially incorporate the `/graph` functionality if that gets implemented first.
